skill.name: devops-runbooks
skill.description: Operational runbook and procedure documentation specialist. Use when creating incident response procedures, operational playbooks, or system maintenance guides.
skill.summary: Creates structured runbooks for incident response, maintenance, rollback, troubleshooting, and escalation.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: The flagged RUNBOOK.template.md entries are benign placeholders for operational systems, not attempts to target the model system prompt. The SKILL.md backtick finding is inline Markdown around a reference path, not Ruby or shell execution. No semantic prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden command execution was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: The placeholder refers to access for an operational system in a runbook prerequisites checklist. It is not framed as a system prompt or an instruction to the assistant.
The placeholder appears beside another operational access requirement and represents a service or platform name. No prompt override language or assistant-directed instruction is present.
The table labels a credential location for a runbook target system. This is normal documentation templating and does not target the model system prompt.
The backticks are Markdown formatting around the reference file path. There is no Ruby code, shell interpolation, or executable command at this location.

content.value_statement: Operational knowledge often lives in tickets, chat, and memory. This skill turns procedures into structured runbooks for incidents, maintenance, rollback, and escalation.
actual_capabilities: Creates runbooks with overview, prerequisites, quick reference, procedure, verification, rollback, troubleshooting, and escalation sections.
Defines access needs, required tools, credentials locations, key commands, URLs, and contacts.
Documents step-by-step procedures with expected output and verification checks.
Adds rollback steps and rollback verification for failed changes.
Captures troubleshooting scenarios, symptoms, causes, and resolutions.
Builds escalation paths and incident handoff templates.
limitations: It does not execute commands or validate live infrastructure state.
It needs accurate service names, contacts, access paths, and command examples from the user.
It cannot verify credentials, permissions, or dashboard URLs.
Generated procedures require review and testing before production use.

use_cases.title: Prepare On-Call Procedures
use_cases.description: Create a clear incident response runbook for alerts, triage, verification, rollback, and escalation.

use_cases.title: Document Maintenance Tasks
use_cases.description: Turn recurring maintenance work into repeatable steps with prerequisites, commands, expected output, and checks.

use_cases.title: Capture Team Knowledge
use_cases.description: Convert informal operational knowledge into a shared runbook for handoffs, training, and service ownership.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Runbook
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a runbook for restarting SERVICE_NAME. Include prerequisites, commands, expected output, verification, rollback, and escalation.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Incident Playbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a P1 incident runbook for API latency. Include triage steps, dashboards, log checks, customer impact, decision points, and escalation.

prompt_templates.title: Add Rollback and Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this deployment procedure with rollback steps, verification commands, success criteria, failure handling, and expected outputs for each step.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize Multiple Runbooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these runbook notes and convert them into a consistent operational format. Identify missing prerequisites, contacts, commands, and test evidence.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a runbook to rotate database credentials.
output_examples.output: A structured procedure with prerequisites, credential storage notes, rotation steps, verification checks, rollback actions, and escalation contacts.

output_examples.input: A team provides notes for a cache outage response.
output_examples.output: An incident playbook covering alert meaning, dashboards, log checks, remediation choices, success criteria, and handoff details.

output_examples.input: An engineer shares a maintenance checklist for service restarts.
output_examples.output: A repeatable runbook with access requirements, quick commands, step-by-step actions, expected results, and post-change validation.

best_practices: Provide real service names, ownership details, and trusted command examples.
Test every procedure in a safe environment before production use.
Keep rollback, verification, and escalation sections updated after incidents.
anti_patterns: Do not publish commands that nobody has reviewed or tested.
Do not store secrets directly in a runbook.
Do not leave escalation contacts, dashboards, or credential paths as vague placeholders.

faq.question: Does this skill execute operational commands?
faq.answer: No. It creates documentation and templates. Users must review and run commands themselves.

faq.question: Can it create incident response runbooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports triage, verification, remediation, rollback, escalation, and handoff sections.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide service names, triggers, dashboards, commands, expected output, contacts, rollback steps, and known failure modes.

faq.question: Can it document maintenance procedures?
faq.answer: Yes. It can turn recurring maintenance tasks into repeatable steps with checks and expected results.

faq.question: Does it validate production access?
faq.answer: No. It can list required access, but it cannot test permissions or credentials.

faq.question: Should generated runbooks be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams should review, test, and update runbooks before relying on them during incidents.
